core_contributions.title: Autoresearch: a new ML-prediction product built as a 22-layer stack
core_contributions.what: Built the flag-gated Autoresearch product from skeleton to UI: data model and HogQL system table, labeler and dataset templates, sandboxed inference, champion selection, scoring and online validation, REST CRUD and lifecycle actions, agent write surface (feature materialization, artifact store), headless training dispatch, a daily Temporal coordinator, 20 MCP tools, and the list/detail/create scenes.
core_contributions.why_it_matters: It is a whole new product surface where agents train and serve models on customer event data; the deep-read layers show care for the risky parts (caller-authored HogQL under query:read scopes and ClickHouse throttles, per-request sandbox directories, row locks against concurrent live runs, artifact size and path guards).
core_contributions.outcome: 28 PRs over 49 days, 5 major, 3 deep reads at P 12.1-13.0 (#89149, #89154, #89155). He is the top author in the area (role.top_area_leader). Still behind a feature flag with no changelog entry, so user adoption is unproven; one layer (#89155) needed a follow-up fix and 18 of the 28 PRs have no recorded review.

core_contributions.title: Signals inbox and scouts: reliability fixes plus new signal sources
core_contributions.what: 90 PRs on Signals: fixed a ClickHouse visibility race that failed ~10% of new reports, stopped research runs from claiming strangers' PRs (which could comment on and close them), added Datadog errors/alerts/APM/logs as inbox sources, follow-up reports for failed validation checks, an 'Unused features' scout, throttle increases, and many scout-skill docs and UI tweaks.
core_contributions.why_it_matters: Two of these are data-correctness / user-harm fixes on a live AI product: #84115 restored report generation, and #86477 (filed under Desktop) prevented the agent from closing unrelated users' PRs. Several shipped as public changelog items.
core_contributions.outcome: Deep reads: #84115 P 13.0 (V3 C3), #86477 P 16.0 (V3 C3). 11 public changelog entries cite 9 of his PRs, including #115135, #115636 and #120323. The tail is long: 39 of 90 PRs are routine or trivial.

core_contributions.title: OAuth incident fix for the ChatGPT connector
core_contributions.what: Let credential-less CIMD private_key_jwt clients fall back to public PKCE on code and refresh grants, added client_auth_method telemetry, and hardened against malformed-assertion downgrades.
core_contributions.why_it_matters: During an active incident every ChatGPT connector token exchange failed with invalid_client and existing connections were breaking as refresh tokens came due; this is an auth-path change where getting the downgrade logic wrong would be a security bug.
core_contributions.outcome: Deep read P 16.0 (V3 C3 N2 L2 Q2, all quotes verified), the joint-highest P in his record; no revert or follow-up fix recorded.

custom_analyses.question: Is his 19/20 delivery position real, or does stacked-PR delivery get compressed by the episode metric?
custom_analyses.why: He ships in numbered stacks (Autoresearch 1/22-22/22, community skills 1/7-7/7), and the delivery column scores max P + 0.25 x rest per episode, which would discount a long stack heavily.
custom_analyses.finding: 29 of his 163 PRs are numbered stack layers (21 in ws2, 7 in ws3, 1 in ws5), and 14 major PRs reduce to 12 major episodes (p15.8). The stratified estimate is 793.1, above the pool median of 616.02, while delivery_hat is 405.78. Compared with tatoalo (delivery 719.31, p73.7), he has fewer PRs (163 vs 344) but more changelog PRs (9 vs 2). The compression is real, but the Autoresearch stack is still flag-gated: none of the 11 changelog entries cites a ws2 PR. Output also front-loads: 141 of 163 PRs landed before the week of 2026-10-05 (which had 1 PR), and the 22 later PRs are mostly routine or trivial.
custom_analyses.effect: delivery 5 -> 6: the matrix undercounts stacks and his incident fixes, but not to 7 because the largest stack has no user-adoption signal yet.

custom_analyses.question: Is his top team_leverage substantive review influence or fast approvals?
custom_analyses.why: team_leverage is 2935.77 (1st), but trust_rank is p10.5 and requested_by is only at the median; the gap needs explaining before grading team.
custom_analyses.finding: Submitted reviews are 315 on 261 PRs (263 APPROVED, 52 COMMENTED, 0 CHANGES_REQUESTED); team_leverage uses metrics.reviews_given = 743, which counts more review events than submitted reviews. Breadth is genuine: 50 authors, 27 teams (1st), first review median 1.53h vs skoob13's 3.71h. Comment reviews cluster on agent-infrastructure (21 of 47 reviews) and unteamed authors (22 of 77); his 30 reviews for ai-research and 34 for surfaces are almost pure approvals (0 and 1 comments). Where he engages, it changes code: on #108760 he left 7 comment reviews on reviewer auto-assignment and research-prompt memory, all on lines changed afterwards. Only 5 people requested him (median). trust_rank is low because his own PRs receive few approvals, not because of his reviewing.
custom_analyses.effect: team 8 -> 7: the reach is real and fast, but approval-dominated with no requested changes and no adoption data, so it reads as an unblocker more than a quality gate.

custom_analyses.question: How much of his own output was independently reviewed, and did the unreviewed part cause problems?
custom_analyses.why: reviews-received covers only 66 PRs, and the dossier red flag lists 4 follow-up-fixed PRs; risk control matters for the quality grade.
custom_analyses.finding: 66 of 163 PRs have a recorded review (83 reviews from 23 reviewers, skoob13 on 27). The 97 without one include 7 of 14 majors (#65013, #87121, #89133, #89149, #89155, #101572, #111518), concentrated in ws1 (55), ws2 (18) and ws3 (14); some stack layers may have been reviewed on a parent PR, which this data cannot show. Despite that, there are 0 reverts and 4 follow-up fixes (#84189, #88990, #89155, #115135), one of them the unreviewed major #89155 (P 13.0). #115135's on-demand deep read (P 4.49, Q1) is a 19-line skill rewrite, so that follow-up looks small. quality_rate is 0.96 (p36.8).
custom_analyses.effect: quality stays at 6: the outcome record is clean, but low review coverage on major work means nobody besides him gated much of it.

custom_analyses.question: Do the high-tier PRs that were never deep-read hold up?
custom_analyses.why: Several majors were only triaged, not deep-read; the strongest claims should not rest on summaries alone.
custom_analyses.finding: Only #84115 confirmed as top-band (P 13.0, V3 C3: the summary workflow read ClickHouse before the embedding insert landed). The other triaged majors deep-read as moderate: #65013 P 5.53, #120323 P 4.49, #95970 P 3.65, #101572 P 3.65. So the major-tier label overstates several feature PRs; his real peaks are the incident fixes (#80746, #86477, #84115) plus the Autoresearch core layers (#89149, #89154, #89155).
custom_analyses.effect: delivery held at 6 rather than 7: half the major tier is moderate on deep read, so the peaks are fewer than the tier counts suggest.

insights.insight: He ships in long numbered stacks (29 of 163 PRs), which makes PR counts look inflated and episode-based delivery look deflated at the same time; neither number alone describes him.

His highest-value work is reactive production fixes on agent products (OAuth for ChatGPT, report-generation race, PR mis-attribution), each P 13-16, rather than the large new feature builds, which deep-read at P 3.6-5.5 apart from the Autoresearch core layers.

He is the main approver for the self-driving and adjacent AI teams (59 self-driving PRs, 30 ai-research, 27 agent-infrastructure), so he functions as an unblocker for the agent org, while his own work is reviewed mostly by one person (skoob13, 27 PRs).
Output dropped after the end of September: the week of 2026-10-05 has 1 PR, and October to November is 22 PRs that are mostly routine or trivial, apart from #120323 and #119301.

red_flags.flag: Four of his PRs needed an explicit follow-up fix (peer.followup_fixed = 4), three of them AI co-authored (metrics.ai_reverted_or_fixed = 3), including the major Autoresearch lifecycle-actions layer.
97 of 163 PRs, including 7 majors, have no recorded review in the data; parent-PR review of stack layers cannot be ruled out.

counter_evidence: Against a higher grade: the matrix places him 19/20 on delivery and 18/20 on trust_rank; half of his triaged majors deep-read as moderate (P 3.6-5.5); Autoresearch is still flag-gated with no changelog entry; his reviews include no changes-requested. Against a lower grade: the episode metric discounts his stacks (stratified 793.1 vs 405.78), he has three incident-class fixes at P 13-16 with no reverts, and he is first in the pool on review reach. Self-description vs behaviour: PR summaries describe Autoresearch as enabling the product's primary flows, but peer behaviour (no changelog citation, 18 of 28 PRs with no recorded review) shows nothing yet beyond the flag. Data caveat: dossier review comments on #120672 read like author replies ('Fixed in ...') and #120672 is in neither his PR list nor reviews.json, so the comment attribution may be mixed with pushes to others' branches (events_given.continue = 302).
